sections.html:
Two separate protections share the name: a property tax exemption under Title 68 and a creditor protection for the home under Title 31. A seller may have one, both or neither, and each is claimed differently.

The tax exemption is a filing with the county assessor that lowers the yearly bill. The Title 31 homestead is not filed anywhere. It is a legal shield that protects a principal residence from forced sale by most creditors, within acreage limits.

sections.h2: What the property tax exemption takes off the bill
sections.html:
It exempts the first $1,000 of assessed value from ad valorem tax. In Oklahoma County that works out to a saving of roughly $87 to $141, so the amount is modest and depends on local millage.

A second $1,000 of assessed value is exempt for a household with gross income from all sources of $30,000 or less. In Oklahoma County that application is renewed each year until the owner reaches age 65.

sections.h2: Questions on the state application form
sections.html:
Form 921 asks questions that decide eligibility, and a no to the wrong one can end the claim. It wants to know whether any part of the property is rented, whether any is used commercially, whether the owner holds only a partial interest, whether it sits in a trust, and whether the home is a manufactured home.

  • Did you own the property on or before January 1?
  • Did you live in it as your residence on January 1?
  • Will your deed be on record with the county clerk on or before February 1?
  • Do you have, or did you have last year, a homestead exemption elsewhere?

An application filed after March 15, or one with a no in the ownership section, may only count toward the following year.

sections.h2: Senior valuation limitation and what happens at sale
sections.html:
The limitation locks the taxable fair cash value of the home for an owner who is 65 or older, is the head of household and has income within the HUD qualifying limit. The limit is $90,300 for the 2026 tax year in Tulsa County, while Oklahoma County's 2025 notice cited $89,500, so the number changes by year.

It does not freeze the tax bill itself. The amount can still rise if the excise board adds millage, a judgment is taken against the county, or voters change assessment percentages.

The limitation ends when title is transferred. A buyer starts fresh, and a seller who is moving does not carry it to the next house automatically.

sections.h2: Applying again after buying a homestead
sections.html:
A new owner has to apply again, because any purchaser or new owner must file an application and the seller's exemption does not pass with the deed.

The statute also puts a duty on the seller side. A taxpayer must tell the assessor in writing about a change in use, and recording a deed or other instrument showing a change of ownership counts as sufficient notice. Owners who keep an exemption they no longer qualify for owe twice the unpaid taxes plus interest and penalty, face a lien, and lose the right to a homestead exemption on any Oklahoma property for two years.

Under 31 O.S. 2, an urban homestead may not exceed one acre and a rural homestead may not exceed 160 acres. In a city, at least 75 percent of the floor area of the improvements must be the principal residence, and if more than 25 percent is used for business the exemption is capped at $5,000.

Temporary renting does not change the homestead character as long as the owner has not acquired another homestead. Section 31-1 also treats a manufactured home as exempt when it is the owner's principal residence, with no acreage figure stated there.

These rules decide what a judgment creditor can reach when a house is sold, and they are why title companies ask who lives in the home.

sections.h2: Does a spouse have to sign the deed?
sections.html:
In most cases, yes. Under 16 O.S. 4, a deed, mortgage or contract affecting an exempt homestead, other than a lease of one year or less, must be in writing and signed by both spouses if both are living and neither is divorced or legally separated.

  • An agent may sign for a spouse only if the power of attorney is recorded with the county clerk in the county where the property sits.
  • A deed recorded for ten years with no court challenge on homestead grounds is treated as valid without the spouse's signature.
  • Missing a spouse's signature on a VA-insured purchase does not void it.

Sellers who inherited a house, or who are separated but not divorced, often discover this requirement late in the process.

sections.h2: Free filing and deed fraud protection
sections.html:
Filing the exemption costs nothing, and the Oklahoma County Assessor warns against companies that charge to prepare and file it. That office rejected 190 applications from a title company that used forms not approved by the Oklahoma Tax Commission.

The county clerk also runs a free deed alert service that notifies an owner by text, phone or email when a document is recorded under their name, which helps catch deed tampering. Each county assessor runs its own filing process, so contact the office for the county where the house sits. The March 15 deadline is the same everywhere, but office hours, online portals and field filing days are not.

sections.h2: How the homestead fits into a quick sale
sections.html:
Homestead status touches three parts of a sale: the tax bill that gets prorated at closing, the spouse's signature on the deed, and whether a creditor has any claim on the proceeds. A seller who never filed for the exemption can still sell, but may have paid more tax than needed.

If a sale happens before March 15, the owner who lived there on January 1 can still file the exemption claim, and a late claim only counts toward the next year. Because a new owner starts over, the buyer should file promptly after closing.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to apply for the Oklahoma homestead exemption?
faqs.a: March 15, or within 30 days after a notice of valuation increase, whichever is later. A later application can still be filed, but it counts from the following tax year.

faqs.q: Do I have to reapply for the homestead exemption every year?
faqs.a: No. An owner who was granted the exemption and still lives in the home does not have to reapply. The additional exemption for households at $30,000 or less is the exception, and in Oklahoma County it is refiled yearly until age 65.

faqs.q: Does the homestead exemption transfer to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. Any purchaser or new owner must file their own application. The senior valuation limitation also ends when title is transferred.

faqs.q: How many acres does an Oklahoma homestead cover?
faqs.a: One acre inside a city or town and 160 acres in a rural area, under 31 O.S. 2. In town, the principal residence must make up at least 75 percent of the improvements to avoid the $5,000 cap.

faqs.q: Can I sell my house without my spouse signing?
faqs.a: Generally not if it is your exempt homestead and your spouse is living and not divorced or separated. Section 16-4 requires both signatures, with narrow exceptions such as a recorded power of attorney. Filing for the exemption itself is free with the county assessor.
